turns.t: Good morning, doctor. I'm here, I suppose, because the district nurse said I should be. I'm fine. I'm just tired, and I'm sure it's nothing.
Thank you for coming, Mrs Dixon. Tell me a bit about your situation at home. ~
My husband has dementia. He's been unwell for five years, and it's got worse this past year. I look after him full time. ~
That sounds exhausting. What does a day look like? ~
Up at six to wash him, dress him, give him breakfast, and then I watch him all day. He wanders. I sleep in short bits, on the settee, in case he goes out. ~
How long since you had a proper night's sleep? ~
Oh, months. I don't remember. ~
How's your own health, how are you feeling in yourself? ~
Run down. A bit achy. I haven't had time to think about it. ~
Any low mood, or feeling like you can't cope?
No. I'm not depressed. No, I just get on with it.
Any other health conditions?
High blood pressure, and I had a hysterectomy.
When was the hysterectomy?
Twenty years ago.
What are you taking?
My blood pressure tablet, amlodipine, 5 mg once a day.
Who helps you at home?
Our daughter comes on Sundays. And the carers, for half an hour in the morning. That's all.
Let me check your pulse and pressure. ~
Go on. ~
Pulse 78, blood pressure 144 over 86, weight 61 kilos.
Is that bad? ~
Your pressure is a bit up, which is understandable with stress and little sleep. I'll listen to your chest. ~
Of course.
Your chest is clear, and your heart sounds are normal.
Good. ~
Mrs Dixon, you're doing an enormous job, and you've not had time to look after yourself. I'm not worried about anything physical today, but I'm worried about you. ~
I'm all right, really. ~
I'd like to arrange a blood test, to check your blood count, thyroid and vitamin D, as tiredness can have physical causes.
Fine. ~
And I'd like to arrange a carer's assessment, so the council can offer you respite care, and some days off.
I couldn't leave him. ~
Respite is a rest, so you can keep going. And there's a carers' support group, and a helpline.
I've seen the leaflet. ~
Please use it. If you ever feel you can't cope, feel low or hopeless, ring me straight away.
I will. Thank you, doctor. It's nice to be asked. ~
